figures.caption: Figure 1: Alignment and readouts. Each training pair is a movie frame and the 2 s of EEG recorded against it: a frozen V-JEPA-2 and a linear projection place the frame in a 512-d space, and one of three EEG encoders — differing only in initialisation and depth, in the colours they keep throughout the paper — is trained to meet it there under a soft-target CLIP loss. Dashed taps mark where the two readouts sit: feature encoding ridge-regresses the pooled vector, retrieval scores cosine similarity after the EEG projection.

Figure 2: Top: subject scaling on four readouts (rows: within- and cross-task; columns: probe and retrieval), test release, each cell at its own held-out optimum. Three arms, 3 nested draws per cell; between-draw sd (≈0.003 probe, ≈0.002 retrieval) is narrower than the plotted lines. Dotted rule and band: the random-encoder floor, per depth; labels give each arm’s terminal score against its own floor. Shaded column: the range covered by prior work. Bottom: where each arm’s optimum sits in measured training compute, one marker per draw, shaded within one noise σ of its peak; hollow markers sit on that cell’s budget (dashed).

Table A11: Probe mean(12) Pearson r for all three arms, test split, each cell at its own held-out optimum. d12r = depth-12 randomly initialised, d22r = depth-22 randomly initialised, d22p = depth-22 initialised from REVE-base; all three are means of 3 draws. ∆d = d22r−d12r (depth at matched initialisation), ∆i = d22p−d22r (initialisation at matched depth).

Table A12: Time-pool e→v top-1 accuracy for all three arms, test split, each cell at its own held-out optimum; columns as in Table A11. Within-task chance is 0.0099 (N = 101); cross-task chance is 0.0118 (N = 85) and the matched random encoder scores 0.012 there – no arm and no S clears it.
